originality.rationale: Hansmann (2026) proves flexible spectral realization with a suitably chosen underlying operator and perturbation, without fixing a factorial compact shift or a sharp functional feasibility threshold; Tcaciuc (2018/2019) gives the degree-one exponential example. The present m>=2 theorem derives sharp bounded coefficients, nilpotence, logarithmic-root stars, spectral-counting and angular density for a prescribed shift. Direct published-finding corpus and accessible-ledger comparisons found no covering claim; earlier entire-function analogues remain a priority risk.

value.rationale: The prescribed exponential secular function has an exact and attained coefficient boundedness boundary; at that boundary a nilpotent rank-one perturbation of a quasinilpotent compact shift creates 2m spectral rays with a sharp O(1)-remainder eigenvalue law and universal weak-Schatten counting ratio 1/pi. The exceptional coupling completely collapses nonzero spectral mass despite unchanged singular-value order. These jointly quantify a natural spectral-component phenomenon beyond textbook existence or a single arbitrary parameter calculation.
